_readme: Track C corpus. NCBI E-utilities, not the reCAPTCHA-gated PMC website. Target is 50+ TER-type labels. 2026-09-24 pass prioritized reviews; the classic review tables are not in PMC and are recorded as blocked. The new plain-text labels are from Hettinga et al. 1997 (8 concentration TERs). They are not in seed_data.py because those cell lines are not in the curated table, and a new cell line needs a real mutation list.

candidates.title: The effect of physiological and supraphysiological temperatures on in vitro and in vivo cytotoxicity of hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy
candidates.access_route: pmc_efetch (main article XML; full text + captions confirmed accessible)
candidates.extraction_status: PDF read 2026-09-24 (cells-09-01775.pdf). Heat maps in Figures 2-5 are color gradients without printed cell values, so they were not converted into numbers. Plain-text TERs now in seed where the sentence names both the temperature and a curated cell line: carboplatin RKO 2.5/3.8/7.2 at 41/42/43C; oxaliplatin 3.3 (RKO) and 3.1 (HCT116) at 43C. Cisplatin '3.5, 2.8, and 3.9 in RKO, HCT116, and COLO320' does not name which temperature those three numbers are, so they stay out of the interaction table. 5-FU TER was not increased (no number). MMC 2D TER was not increased. Organoid and RT112 numbers are below.

plain_text_labels.quote: increased at higher temperatures starting at 41C to 3.5, 2.8, and 3.9 in RKO, HCT116, and COLO320 respectively (Figure S4). Stored at 43C, the top of the stated range.

plain_text_labels.note: COLO320 is not in the curated cell-line table
42C is the organoid hyperthermia temperature in the same paragraph; the TER sentence does not restate it
highest MMC TER at 42C among the bladder lines in Figure S5C; the other lines in that panel are not given as numbers

candidates.relevance: Same paper as the 5 existing real labels; figures 3-4 would multiply real TER coverage across cell lines for the same drugs.

candidates.title: Enhancement of the cytotoxicity of radiosensitizers by modest hyperthermia: the electron-affinity relationship
candidates.authors: Rajaratnam S, Adams GE, Stratford IJ, Clarke C
candidates.access_route: pmc_efetch (confirmed, full text retrieved, CC-BY)
candidates.extraction_status: extracted, deliberately NOT added to seed_data.py -- real time-to-isoeffect enhancement values found (V79-379A cells, hypoxic, equitoxic concentrations, 34/37/41C): metronidazole (30mM) needed 12h at 37C vs 6h at 41C for the same survival level (10^-2) -> 2.0x time-reduction enhancement; misonidazole (2mM) needed 8h at 37C vs 6h at 41C -> 1.33x; nitrofurantoin (100uM) showed no thermal enhancement at all (34-41C). NOT integrated into seed_data.py because none of these three drugs (radiosensitizers/hypoxic cytotoxins) are in this project's curated DRUGS list, which is scoped to standard chemotherapeutics -- adding new drug entries is a scope decision, not made unilaterally here. Also a different metric type again (time-to-isoeffect ratio, not TER/IC50-fold-shift/ER) -- would need its own explicit tag per the build order's metric-homogeneity rule.
candidates.relevance: Radiosensitizer + mild hyperthermia class, adjacent to the thermal TER literature per the build order's own framing.

candidates.title: Haematological toxicity of carboplatin and cisplatin combined with whole body hyperthermia in rats
candidates.access_route: pmc_efetch (confirmed, full text retrieved)
candidates.extraction_status: extracted, deliberately NOT added to seed_data.py -- real TERs are all systemic-toxicity endpoints (F344 rat, whole-body hyperthermia 2h/41.5C): carboplatin thrombocytopenia=2.0, anaemia=2.8, leukopenia=1.9; cisplatin thrombocytopenia=1.8, anaemia=2.4, leukopenia=1.9. These are NOT tumor-cytotoxicity/efficacy TERs and do not fit interaction_effect.combined_effect_metric (which represents anti-tumor synergy -- a high toxicity TER is a bad outcome, the opposite polarity). Recorded here as real values for a future toxicity-aware schema extension, not forced into the current efficacy-only schema.
candidates.relevance: Real TER values, directly stated in text -- cheap extraction once prioritized.

candidates.title: Mechanism of hyperthermic potentiation of cisplatin action in cisplatin-sensitive and -resistant tumour cells
candidates.access_route: pmc_efetch full text (CC; OCR of a scanned BJC article, numbers below read from the running text)
candidates.extraction_status: extracted 2026-09-24. Eight concentration TERs are plain text. Not added to seed_data.py: EN/ER are murine Ehrlich-derived lines and GLC4/GLC4-cDDP are human small-cell lines, none of them in the curated cell-line table. Adding a line would require a real mutation list (tests reject an empty one). Metric is the paper's own definition: cisplatin concentration that kills 90% of cells at 37C, divided by the concentration that kills 90% when heat is given during the first part of a 90 min drug exposure. Curves were corrected for heat-alone killing. At 43C, CEM43 in minutes equals the heat duration; that conversion is derived here, not reported by the paper.

candidates.title: Cisplatin sensitivity and thermochemosensitisation in thermotolerant cDDP-sensitive and -resistant cell lines
candidates.access_route: pmc_efetch full text
candidates.extraction_status: PDF read 2026-09-24 (brjcancer00049-0072.pdf). Absolute TERs are plotted in Figure 7 and are not printed. The text gives reduction factors for both 30 and 60 min at 43C: 2.1 in sensitive EN cells and 1.6 in resistant ER cells. The discussion states 2.09±0.14 (EN) versus 1.59±0.10 (ER). These factors are not a 30-min versus 60-min split. ER cells are also 4.8 times more cisplatin-resistant than EN cells at 37C; that 4.8 is a resistance factor, not a TER.
candidates.relevance: Same EN/ER lines as PMID 9192975. Useful once the figures are digitized; the plain text does not give a standalone TER.

candidates.title: Thermochemotherapy: synergism between hyperthermia (42-43 degrees) and adriamycin (or bleomycin) in mammalian cell inactivation
candidates.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
candidates.authors: Hahn GM, Braun J, Har-Kedar I
candidates.access_route: pmc record exists; publisher blocks full-text XML. Abstract only.
candidates.extraction_status: PDF read 2026-09-24 (pnas00046-0167.pdf). No classic TER is printed. Two single-dose survival comparisons are. Bleomycin is not a curated drug. EMT-6 and HA1 are not curated cell lines, so neither number is in seed.

plain_text_labels.quote: predicted survival for combined exposure should be about 20%. In fact, the measured survival is 4e-4, lower by a factor of 500
At 30 mg/kg, the combined effect has reduced survival to about 10^-4. Heat alone: about 40% survive. Drug alone does not exceed 80% killing.

candidates.relevance: Foundational doxorubicin/bleomycin paper. The printed comparisons are single-dose survival ratios, not TERs.
